objective_pt: Challenge an argument, rebut a point and defend your position politely but firmly ("That's a fair point, but...", "I'd take issue with...", "The evidence suggests otherwise").

teacher.goal_pt: Get the learner arguing about a light topic and notice how they disagree.
prompts: Pineapple on pizza: yes or no? Convince me.
What's the strongest argument against your view?
watchFor: "I don't agree with you" as the only option; introduce "I see it differently".
"I agree with you" pronounced as "I am agree" (from "eu concordo").

exercises.prompt: That's a fair point, but I see it differently.
accepted: That's a fair point, but I see it differently
That is a fair point but I see it differently

exercises.instruction_pt: Which is the most natural way to disagree in a formal debate?
options: I am not agree with this.
With all due respect, I'd take issue with that claim.
exercises.explanation_pt: "With all due respect" plus "take issue with" is firm but polite. "I am not agree" is a typical Brazilian error: "agree" is a verb, so "I don't agree".

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Eu discordo totalmente."
accepted: I totally disagree
I completely disagree
I strongly disagree
I disagree completely
I disagree entirely
I couldn't disagree more
I entirely disagree
I fully disagree

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Agree" and "disagree" are verbs, so don't use "am": "I disagree", not "I am disagree".

teacher.goal_pt: Language for rebuttal: take issue with, concede, counterargument, hold water, the burden of proof.
prompts: Which popular belief do you think doesn't hold water?
Can you concede one point to someone you disagree with?
watchFor: "Argument" used to mean "discussion" only; in English it can also mean a fight.
"Discuss about" (from "discutir sobre"); "discuss" takes a direct object.

exercises.example_en: I'd take issue with the idea that money buys happiness.
That theory doesn't really hold water.

exercises.meaning_pt: admitir, reconhecer (um ponto do outro lado)
exercises.example_en: I'll concede that the costs are high.

exercises.instruction_pt: Match each debating expression with its meaning.
Say this in natural English: "Vamos discutir esse ponto."
accepted: Let's discuss this point
Let's discuss that point
Let's talk about this point
Let's talk about that point
Let's go over this point
Let's look at this point
Let's discuss this

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Discuss" takes a direct object: "discuss this point", never "discuss about". ("Talk about" does take "about".)

teacher.goal_pt: Use contrastive stress to highlight the point you are challenging.
prompts: Say "I didn't say it was EASY, I said it was POSSIBLE."
Which word would you stress to challenge the number in "Most people agree"?
watchFor: Even stress on every word, so the contrast disappears.
Adding a vowel to final consonants: "issue-e", "point-chi".

exercises.instruction_pt: Repeat, stressing "cause" and "symptom" to contrast them.
exercises.prompt: That's not the cause, it's a symptom.
accepted: That's not the cause, it's a symptom
That is not the cause, it is a symptom

exercises.instruction_pt: Repeat. "Doesn't" is stressed; "hold water" links smoothly.
exercises.prompt: With respect, that argument doesn't hold water.
accepted: With respect, that argument doesn't hold water
With respect, that argument does not hold water

exercises.instruction_pt: In "I said SOME people, not ALL people", why are "some" and "all" stressed?
options: Because they are at the start of a phrase.
exercises.explanation_pt: English uses stress to mark contrast. Stressing the words you are correcting makes your rebuttal clear.

teacher.goal_pt: Follow the structure of an argument (claim, concession, rebuttal) and respond to it.
prompts: What was their main point after "but"?
watchFor: Focusing on the concession and missing the real point after "but" or "however".
Replying "I agree" without saying with what.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen. What is the speaker's main point?
exercises.listen: Admittedly, public transport is expensive to build. But in the long run, it saves cities far more than it costs.
options: Public transport pays off over time.
Cities should stop building public transport.
exercises.explanation_pt: "Admittedly" introduces a concession; the main point comes after "But": it saves more than it costs.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen and rebut the claim politely, starting with a concession.
exercises.listen: Social media has done more harm than good.
accepted: That's a fair point, but it has also connected people
I see your point, but it has also brought people together
That may be true, but it has some real benefits
That's true to some extent, but it has benefits too
I take your point, but it also has benefits
You have a point, but it has helped a lot of people
Fair point, but it has also done a lot of good
I see what you mean, but it has also done a lot of good
Maybe, but it has also done a lot of good

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Você tem razão" is "You're right" or "You have a point", not "you have reason".
commonErrors.correction_en: You have a point, but it has also done a lot of good.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Agree" is a verb: "I agree" / "I don't agree".
commonErrors.correction_en: I don't entirely agree. It has also done a lot of good.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen and ask the speaker to back up their claim.
exercises.listen: Everyone knows that young people don't read anymore.
accepted: What evidence do you have for that?
Where's the evidence for that?
Is there any evidence for that?
What makes you say that?
What's that based on?
Do you have any data to back that up?
Can you back that up?
How do you know that?
What's your evidence?
Says who?

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Evidence" is uncountable in English: "some evidence", "any evidence", never "evidences".
commonErrors.correction_en: What evidence do you have for that?

commonErrors.explanation_pt: The noun is "proof" (uncountable) or "evidence"; "proves" is a verb form.
commonErrors.correction_en: What evidence do you have for that?

teacher.goal_pt: Run a short structured debate: claim, support, concession, rebuttal, conclusion.
prompts: Should university be free for everyone?
I'll play devil's advocate. What would you say to someone who says it's too expensive?
Can you sum up your position in one sentence?
watchFor: Personal attacks or overly direct language ("You're wrong").

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Concordo em parte, mas acho que você está ignorando os custos."
accepted: I partly agree, but I think you're ignoring the costs
I agree up to a point, but I think you're ignoring the costs
I agree to some extent, but I think you're ignoring the costs
I partially agree, but I think you're ignoring the costs
I partly agree, but I think you're overlooking the costs
I agree in part, but I think you're ignoring the costs
I agree with you in part, but I think you're overlooking the costs

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Agree" is a verb: "I partly agree", not "I am partly agree".
commonErrors.correction_en: I partly agree, but I think you're ignoring the costs.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Em parte" is "in part" or "partly" (singular), not "in parts".
commonErrors.correction_en: I partly agree, but I think you're ignoring the costs.

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Só para bancar o advogado do diabo: e se isso não funcionar?"
accepted: Just to play devil's advocate, what if it doesn't work?
Just to play devil's advocate, what if this doesn't work?
Just to play devil's advocate, what if that doesn't work?
To play devil's advocate, what if it doesn't work?
Playing devil's advocate, what if it doesn't work?
Let me play devil's advocate. What if it doesn't work?

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "E se...?" is "What if...?" in English. "And if..." sounds incomplete.
commonErrors.correction_en: Just to play devil's advocate, what if it doesn't work?

commonErrors.explanation_pt: The fixed expression is "devil's advocate", not "devil's lawyer".
commonErrors.correction_en: Just to play devil's advocate, what if it doesn't work?

exercises.instruction_pt: Put the words in order to concede a point.
accepted: I'll grant you that it's expensive

exercises.instruction_pt: Respond to the claim in about a minute, as if in a debate.
exercises.prompt_en: Here's my position: university education should be completely free for everyone. Convince me I'm wrong, or tell me why I'm right.
guidelines_pt: State your position clearly in the first sentence.
Concede one point: "I'll grant you that...".
Rebut with a reason and, if possible, evidence.

teacher.goal_pt: Recycle rebuttal language and the key grammar traps (agree, discuss, evidence).
prompts: Disagree with me politely: "Cats are better than dogs."

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Esse argumento não se sustenta."
accepted: That argument doesn't hold water
This argument doesn't hold water
That argument doesn't stand up
That argument doesn't hold up
This argument doesn't hold up
That argument doesn't stand up to scrutiny
That argument is not convincing

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Sustentar-se" (an argument) is "hold water" or "hold up". "Sustain itself" is a literal translation.

exercises.sentence: There isn't enough ___ to support that claim.
accepted: evidence
proof
data

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Evidence" and "proof" are uncountable here: no plural.
commonErrors.correction_en: There isn't enough evidence to support that claim.

options: I admit you're right about that.
exercises.explanation_pt: "I'll grant you that" is a concession: you admit the other person has a point.

exercises.prompt: All things considered, I stand by what I said.
accepted: All things considered, I stand by what I said
